critical_issues: CRITICAL (metadata back-compat, FALSE additive claim): The spec bumps CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION 2->3 but does NOT amend load_kernel_metadata's version guard. The current guard (crates/axc-runtime/src/metadata.rs:212) is `if meta.schema_version != 1 && meta.schema_version != CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION { reject }`. After the bump to 3 this becomes `!= 1 && != 3` -- which REJECTS every existing version-2 (M3.1 coopmat) sidecar with MetadataSchemaMismatch. The spec's repeated 'v1/v2 sidecars still load' promise is therefore UNIMPLEMENTED by the listed edits. files_to_modify for metadata.rs MUST add an explicit accept-list (1,2,3) and AT-1631 must assert a literal v2 sidecar loads after the bump. This is a real, shipping back-compat regression as written.

CRITICAL (existing test WILL break -- contradicts AT-1611 additive-only guarantee): crates/axc-runtime/tests/metadata_roundtrip.rs:126 hardcodes `MetadataSchemaMismatch { got: 99, supported: 2 }`. Bumping CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION to 3 changes `supported` to 3 and this assertion FAILS. The spec claims 'existing tests stay green / additive-only' but this test (and any other hardcoding supported:2) MUST be edited. The files_to_modify list omits metadata_roundtrip.rs. The Coder will hit a red test the plan said would be green.

CRITICAL (coopmat-load-from-shared access-chain): emit_coopmat_load_inline / emit_coopmat_store_inline (crates/axc-codegen/src/coopmat.rs:235,279) build a TWO-INDEX access chain `access_chain(elem_ptr_ty, None, buf_var, [zero_id, element_offset_id])` because the SSBO wraps its array in OpTypeStruct (confirmed buffers.rs:111). A Workgroup shared array has NO wrapping struct, so a shared-source coopmat load MUST use a SINGLE-index chain `[element_offset_id]` with a Workgroup-class elem_ptr_ty. The spec (B.2) says 'a parallel path' but does NOT mandate a SEPARATE function nor forbid threading a `zero_id` into the shared path. If the Coder reuses emit_coopmat_load_inline with a Workgroup ptr type and the [zero,offset] index list, spirv-val will reject (or worse, miscompute the offset). REQUIRE: an explicit, separate Shared-source emit that uses a one-element index list, with an AT asserting the shared-coopmat OpAccessChain has exactly ONE index operand (parallel to AT-1608).

CRITICAL (runtime preflight underspecified + wrong location): The spec says 'prepare_kernel_checked reads VkPhysicalDeviceLimits.maxComputeSharedMemorySize'. But (a) prepare_kernel_checked lives in context.rs:871 (NOT dispatch.rs as files_to_modify claims), (b) VulkanContext does NOT currently cache maxComputeSharedMemorySize -- context.rs:626 caches only max_compute_work_group_count and non_coherent_atom_size; the new limit must be plumbed at init (Step 8), (c) prepare_kernel_checked's signature takes only `coopmat: Option<&CoopMatShapeMeta>` and preflight_kernel_support has no shared-bytes parameter -- the spec does not state how shared_memory_bytes reaches the preflight (new param? read from a KernelMetadata threaded in?). As written the preflight is not wireable. SPECIFY the exact signature change and the context-field addition.
warnings: WARNING (barrier oracle is NOT load-bearing on Lavapipe -- the AT-1606 proof is weaker than claimed): Lavapipe (Mesa llvmpipe) executes workgroup invocations largely SERIALLY on CPU threads; a missing WorkgroupMemory barrier frequently does NOT manifest a visible race there (same false-pass class as NVIDIA warp-lockstep). So AT-1606's barrier-present variant passing on Lavapipe does NOT prove the barrier is load-bearing -- the without-barrier variant may ALSO pass on Lavapipe. The spec already declines to assert the no-barrier variant bit-exact (good), but it should NOT claim AT-1606 'PROVES the barrier is load-bearing on the dev GPU' for CI. The only real proof is on hardware with independent SIMD lanes (NVIDIA subgroup-32, ideally AMD wave64). Demand AT-1606 record that the load-bearing assertion is HARDWARE-gated (NVIDIA at minimum), with Lavapipe providing only the warning-emission + bit-exact-with-barrier half. The cross-vendor race proof (AMD/Intel) remains an untested gap (EB.1) and must be labeled as such, NOT implied-covered.

WARNING (double-buffer / loop-carried tile hazard): The K-loop matmul needs TWO barriers per iteration -- one AFTER staging-write (visibility) and one AFTER the coopmat read but BEFORE the next iteration overwrites the staging arrays (anti-WAR). B.1 steps 2 and 4 DO specify both. Good. But the advisory SharedWriteWithoutBarrierBeforeRead lint is straight-line only and will NOT catch the loop-carried WAR (write of iter k+1 racing read of iter k) because that hazard spans a back-edge. Note explicitly that the lint cannot see this; the second barrier is correctness-critical and rests entirely on the hand-written kernel + the AT-1620 bit-exact GPU check. Ensure AT-1620 uses a K large enough (>= 2 TILE_K blocks) to actually exercise the loop-carried barrier (a single-K-block fixture would pass even with the second barrier missing).

WARNING (caps.float16 not auto-set by observe_type): body.rs:213 observe_type maps I8/U8->int8, I16/U16->int16, I64/U64->int64, F64->float64, but F16 falls into `_ => {}` and does NOT set float16. So a standalone shared[f16,N] with no coopmat/no f16-SSBO will emit f16 OpLoad/OpStore WITHOUT OpCapability Float16 unless emit.rs explicitly sets caps.float16 from the shared-decl scan. The spec's emit.rs change states this, but the Coder must NOT assume observe_type covers it. AT-1609 must include the no-SSBO/no-coopmat shared[f16] case and assert spirv-val rejects the missing-cap build (or that the cap is present).

WARNING (divergent barrier in the SHIPPED kernels): Divergent-context tracking already EXISTS (typecheck.rs:545 divergent_context_depth; validate.rs:185 warns subgroup ops in divergent context) -- so the claim 'M3.2 does not add it / out of scope' coexists with infrastructure that could cheaply flag a barrier in divergent flow. The reduction oracle (shared_reduce.axc) and matmul both put barriers inside loops; the reduction's tree step is the canonical place a barrier gets mistakenly nested inside `if (lid < stride)`. Since OpControlBarrier in non-uniform flow is UB, and the lint machinery already exists, RECOMMEND a minimal hard check: workgroup_barrier() must not appear at divergent_context_depth>0 (loop bodies that ALL invocations enter are uniform and OK; if/else bodies are not). At minimum, every shipped M3.2 kernel must be manually audited and a comment must assert each barrier is in uniform control flow.

WARNING (shr/>> in reduction oracle): The canonical tree reduction uses `stride >>= 1`. Anti-pattern #8 bans `>>`; existing code uses lshr() (q4km examples). The shared_reduce.axc oracle MUST use lshr()/shr(), not `>>`. Trivial but the Coder copies CUDA idioms -- flag it.

WARNING (Workgroup OpVariable uninitialized + write-before-read): The design correctly emits no initializer (Vulkan forbids it without VK_KHR_zero_initialize_workgroup_memory). But this means any kernel that READS a shared cell before WRITING it reads garbage. The reduction and matmul stage-then-barrier-then-read, so they write-before-read by construction -- but there is NO compiler check that every read-index was previously written. This is acceptable for M3.2 (undecidable in general) but should be documented as a known sharp edge alongside the barrier lint.

WARNING (bank conflicts -- perf only, noted): shared[f16, TILE*TILE] with no padding will bank-conflict on the 32-bank model for power-of-two tile widths (the @shared_tile(pad=K) sugar that fixes it is DEFERRED). Not a correctness issue; will depress the PART B TFLOPS number. Acceptable to defer but the honest TFLOPS report should not be surprised by sub-peak numbers attributable to conflicts.

WARNING (AT-1622 hole-genuineness can be gamed): Comparing tile_k=16 vs 32 OpTypeArray length constants proves the array SIZE differs, but does NOT alone prove the holes drive the COMPUTE (a kernel could size the array differently yet loop a fixed number of times). The AT must ALSO assert the K-loop trip-count / OpLoop structure differs AND that a bit-exact GPU result holds for BOTH tile_k values (so a larger array that is under-iterated would produce a wrong result and fail). Size-diff alone is necessary but not sufficient to refute the M3.1.5 inert-holes failure mode.
principle_violations: NONE FATAL. Anti-pattern #1 (no inference): N pinned to an unsuffixed literal, holes substituted as source text upstream -- intact. #2 explicit returns: examples must carry `return;` (audit the new .axc). #6 graceful recovery: new ParseError variants + recover-to ;/} specified. #7 no silent capability: Workgroup needs no new cap/ext; f16->Float16 ONLY, i8->Int8 ONLY, explicitly NOT StorageBuffer8/16BitAccess -- correct per SPIR-V (those KHR caps gate the StorageBuffer storage class, not Workgroup). #9 real GPU: AT-1606/1620/1621/1630 are #[ignore]-gated real-GPU tests, no mock. The only soft concern is the warning-not-error severity for missing-barrier (OQ1) -- defensible given undecidability, but see OQ position below.
spirv_concerns: OpTypeArray length MUST be the <id> of an OpConstant (SPIR-V 3.32.6), not a literal -- spec says so (get_or_emit_u32_const). Correct.

Single-index OpAccessChain into a Workgroup OpTypeArray is correct (no wrapping struct); the SSBO two-index form (struct-member-0 then array index) must NOT be copied. The coopmat-from-shared path is the high-risk spot (see CRITICAL #3).

OpControlBarrier scope=Workgroup(2)/Workgroup(2)/semantics=0x108 (AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory) is VERIFIED in actual code (codegen/src/subgroup.rs:34,298-300; test asserts scope 2/2 and semantics 0x108 at lines 517-519). The memory-semantics for cross-invocation Workgroup visibility is correct per the Vulkan memory model: a single barrier with WorkgroupMemory acq-rel between the write phase and read phase IS sufficient for the straight-line stage->barrier->read pattern. For the LOOPED matmul, a single barrier is NOT sufficient -- two are needed (write-visibility + WAR-protection), which B.1 provides.

Workgroup OpVariable excluded from the SPIR-V 1.3 OpEntryPoint interface list (only Input/Output) -- correct for 1.3; would CHANGE in SPIR-V 1.4+ (all global vars listed), but the repo pins 1.3 (CURRENT_SPIRV_VERSION guard). Fine while pinned; add a forward-compat note.

OpCooperativeMatrixLoadKHR from a Workgroup-class pointer: the SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix spec DOES permit Workgroup/StorageBuffer/PhysicalStorageBuffer pointer operands, and the op is storage-class-agnostic. The risk is NOT the op -- it is the access-chain pointer TYPE and index arity (CRITICAL #3). Also confirm the coopmat 'stride' semantics for a row-major tile staged in a flat shared array match what was loaded (stride in ELEMENTS of the shared array row, which may differ from the SSBO row stride).
vendor_concerns: The whole feature's #1 hazard IS vendor heterogeneity: a missing barrier passes on NVIDIA (subgroup-32 lockstep) AND on Lavapipe (serial CPU emulation) but RACES on AMD wave64 / Intel where the workgroup spans multiple independent SIMD groups. CI has only Lavapipe + (self-hosted) NVIDIA -- NEITHER reliably exposes the race. The design must NOT claim the barrier correctness is 'proven' cross-vendor; it is proven correct-WITH-barrier and the no-barrier race is documented (EB.1), not tested. This is the single most dangerous hole.

PART B coopmat path requires subgroup_size==32 (context.rs:234 NVIDIA-32 assumption); AMD wave64 / Intel variable subgroup graceful-skip via CoopMatUnsupported -- consistent with M3.1, fine. The f32 shared-staged variant (matmul_shared_f32.axc) is the cross-vendor parity proof and does NOT need coopmat -- good, but it does NOT exercise the coopmat-from-shared access-chain path (CRITICAL #3), so that path is NVIDIA-only-tested.

maxComputeSharedMemorySize varies wildly: Vulkan min 16384, NVIDIA up to ~99KiB opt-in, AMD 64KiB LDS, mobile often exactly 16384. The static 65536 hard-error ceiling will let a kernel compile that then preflight-skips on a 32KiB-or-less device. Acceptable (fail-closed skip), but the >16384 'portable minimum' warning is the right knob -- ensure it actually fires.
missing_tests: MUST TEST: a literal version-2 (M3.1 coopmat) sidecar JSON loads successfully AFTER the v3 bump (back-compat regression guard for CRITICAL #1). AT-1631 mentions it -- make it assert against a hand-written v2 JSON, not just a serde default.
MUST UPDATE: metadata_roundtrip.rs AT-513 hardcoded `supported: 2` -> 3 (CRITICAL #2). List it in files_to_modify.
MUST TEST: shared-source coopmat OpAccessChain has EXACTLY ONE index operand and Workgroup storage class (parallel to AT-1608) -- the byte-level guard for CRITICAL #3.

MUST TEST: existing q4km_dequant_matmul_coopmat.axc SPIR-V is BYTE-IDENTICAL after adding the CoopMatLoadSource discriminator (the M3.1 regression guard the architect's OQ5 asks for). AT-1611 is generic; add an explicit coopmat byte-identity fixture.
MUST TEST: AT-1620 matmul fixture uses K spanning >= 2 TILE_K blocks so the loop-carried (second) barrier is actually load-bearing; a 1-block fixture would pass with it removed.
MUST TEST: AT-1606 load-bearing claim is HARDWARE-gated (NVIDIA), with Lavapipe asserting only warning-emission + bit-exact-with-barrier (Lavapipe cannot prove the race).
MUST TEST: standalone shared[f16,N] with no coopmat and no f16 SSBO emits OpCapability Float16 (observe_type does NOT cover F16 -- body.rs:213).

MUST TEST: 50GB memory cap -- the 4096x4096 f16 matmul bench allocates ~3 x 32MiB (A,B,C f16) ~ 96MiB, fine; but confirm the resident bench does not accumulate per-dispatch allocations across the N-dispatch loop (upload-once is claimed -- verify no per-iter staging leak).
questions_for_architect: OQ1 (warning vs error for missing barrier): I accept WARNING for the general/loop-carried case (undecidable, cross-iteration). But for the PROVABLE straight-line single-block case the lint already detects (SharedWrite of id X, then SharedRead of id X, no intervening Barrier, same block, no back-edge), why not make THAT specific case a HARD error? It is decidable, it is exactly the NVIDIA-passes/AMD-races trap, and a hard error there costs nothing in false positives. Recommend: hard error for the straight-line same-block provable case; warning elsewhere. At minimum, justify why even the provable case stays advisory.

OQ2 (divergent barrier): Given divergent_context_depth ALREADY exists in typecheck.rs, adding 'workgroup_barrier() at depth>0 in an if/else (non-uniform) body is an error' is cheap and closes a real UB. Why defer it when the new kernels are precisely the ones that loop+barrier? Loop bodies all-invocations-enter are uniform (OK); the guard only needs to flag if/else-nested barriers. Please reconsider landing the minimal check in M3.2.

OQ3 (maxComputeSharedMemorySize ceiling): 65536 fixed is fine for M3.2, but plumb the DEVICE limit at preflight (CRITICAL #4) -- the compile-time 65536 must not be the only gate, or a 16KiB-min mobile device pipeline-create-crashes. Confirm the preflight is wired before claiming graceful skip.

OQ4 (FA2 labeling honesty): C1 is NON-streaming full-softmax tiled attention. That is NOT FlashAttention-2 -- FA2's DEFINING contribution IS the online/streaming softmax + the work-partitioning that avoids materializing the SxS scores. Calling C1 'FlashAttention-2' in DESIGN.md / ROADMAP / changelog is a MISLABEL that risks a reward-hacked 'we shipped FA2' claim. Require: C1 is labeled 'tiled (non-streaming) attention -- FA2 C1 prerequisite'; the 'FlashAttention-2' name is reserved until C2 (streaming softmax) lands in M3.2b. The milestone TITLE 'shared-fa2' should be softened. Also: C1 materializes the full score row in shared/registers -- for seq_len=64 fine, but it does NOT scale to FA2's regime, so any TFLOPS framing for C1 would be doubly misleading (none is claimed -- keep it that way).
summary: NEEDS_REVISION. The core language-feature design is sound and well-grounded in the actual codebase: the workgroup_barrier() memory semantics (scope=Workgroup(2), 0x108=AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory) are VERIFIED correct in codegen/src/subgroup.rs and are sufficient for the straight-line stage->barrier->read pattern; the single-index Workgroup access chain, no-initializer Workgroup OpVariable, capability minimality (Float16/Int8/Int16 only, no StorageBuffer8/16BitAccess), and interface-list exclusion are all SPIR-V-correct for the pinned 1.3 target; the K-loop matmul correctly specifies BOTH barriers (write-visibility + WAR). However FOUR critical, shipping-blocking holes must be fixed first: (1) the v2->v3 metadata bump as specified REJECTS existing v2 sidecars (the version guard at metadata.rs:212 is not amended) -- the 'v1/v2 still load' promise is unimplemented; (2) the additive-only claim is FALSE -- metadata_roundtrip.rs AT-513 hardcodes supported:2 and WILL break; (3) the coopmat-load-from-shared path must NOT reuse the SSBO two-index access chain (coopmat.rs:235,279) -- a Workgroup array needs a single-index chain, and this NVIDIA-only-tested path needs an explicit separate emit + an arity-assertion AT plus a byte-identity guard for existing Buffer-source coopmat SPIR-V; (4) the maxComputeSharedMemorySize preflight is not wireable as written -- the limit is not cached on VulkanContext (context.rs:626), prepare_kernel_checked lives in context.rs not dispatch.rs, and its signature has no shared-bytes channel. Beyond those: AT-1606 cannot PROVE the barrier is load-bearing on Lavapipe (serial CPU) OR NVIDIA (lockstep) -- the cross-vendor race (AMD wave64/Intel) is the genuine #1 hazard and remains UNTESTED (EB.1), so the design must not imply it is proven; the missing-barrier policy should be a HARD error in the decidable straight-line case; the divergent-barrier check is cheap (infra exists) and the shipped looping kernels are exactly where it bites; and -- the single most dangerous HONESTY hole -- C1 is non-streaming full-softmax tiled attention and must NOT be labeled 'FlashAttention-2' (FA2 IS the streaming softmax), to avoid a reward-hacked 'shipped FA2' claim. Fix the 4 criticals + the FA2 relabel + the AT hardening, and this is approvable.
single_most_dangerous_hole: Cross-vendor shared-memory race correctness is asserted but UNTESTABLE in CI: a missing/insufficient WorkgroupMemory barrier passes on both Lavapipe (serial CPU emulation) and NVIDIA (subgroup-32 lockstep) yet RACES on AMD wave64 / Intel where a workgroup spans independent SIMD groups. AT-1606 therefore does NOT prove the barrier is load-bearing; it proves only bit-exactness WITH the barrier present and that the advisory warning fires. The honest position: the barrier semantics are provably correct on paper (and verified in subgroup.rs), but the empirical race-detection that would catch a Coder's missing-barrier bug requires AMD/Intel hardware the project does not have. Tie this to the FA2-mislabel honesty risk: shipping 'FlashAttention-2' (which is really non-streaming tiled attention) on top of a shared-memory primitive whose race-safety is unprovable in CI is exactly the implicit-claim surface this project exists to eliminate.
